name: Context delivery
summary: What reaches the agent and when: the session-start digest, pinned context, standing rules, context packs, prompt-time recall and compaction.

features.name: Active preferences injection
features.summary: Sessions start with confirmed rules, recent retirements, topic heads and pinned context; subagents skip the last two.
capabilities: Injects confirmed rules, topic heads, pinned context, active.md and lessons.md at session start and compaction
Renders active.md from confirmed and quarantined preferences, a 30-day most-applied top 10 and 3 retirements
Puts stated rules before deduced and inferred ones with `guardrails.provenance_trust_ordering` (default off)
Charges memory to `active.inject_budget_chars` (8000), cutting sections to headlines, then dropping them
Keeps one hook payload under 9000 chars (UTF-8 bytes on Codex), ending it in one truncation note
Adds up to 12 project topic heads (1600 chars) and the pinned context (1200 chars) inside that budget
Sends subagents rules, active.md and lessons.md, no topic heads or pinned context (`subagent-inject`)
Returns the digest, pinned context and counts through `brain_context` for hosts without a SessionStart hook
Delivers parts 2 to 8 of an oversized start payload one per later event (`reground_parts_enabled`, off)
limits: Pushes context only on hosts that run the hooks; other hosts must call brain_context themselves
Topic heads need a brain store and a project linked to the vault; personal topics are never injected
The subagent write-call fallback delivers once per agent id; its ledger keeps the last 200 ids for 24 h

features.name: Pinned context
features.summary: A current-task scratchpad that survives context rotation without becoming a permanent preference.
capabilities: Reads, writes, appends or clears Brain/pinned.md through brain_pinned_context; read is the default
Applies an ordered batch of write, append, clear and exact-text replace operations all or nothing
Refuses content over 20,000 chars with budget_exceeded and a shrink hint instead of truncating it
Serializes writers with a per-file lock and re-reads inside it, so concurrent appends are not lost
Redacts secrets, strips control characters and normalizes to NFC before storing the text
Rides the session-start digest fenced as untrusted text, capped by active.pinned_max_chars (default 1200)
Keeps pinned-set and pinned-clear records in the brain store on a switched machine instead of the file
On a switched machine remote callers use the shared register, refused while the private one holds a record
A local read falls back to the shared register while the private one holds no record
limits: No per-task or per-session pad: one per vault, or one per store register on a switched machine
No CLI verb edits it; only the MCP tool and the post-compaction re-assertion write it

features.name: Standing rules
features.summary: Operator-written rules, vault-wide or scoped to a project, harness or host, delivered to every session.
capabilities: Injects Brain/standing-rules.md first at session start and in subagents, under an outranks-memory header
Caps the vault-wide rules at `active.standing_rules_max_chars` (4000), outside the memory injection budget
Reads it outside the fail-open memory load, never caches it, and says so when the file cannot be read
Adds Brain/standing-rules/{project,harness,host}/<key>.md, capped at 2000 chars and charged to the budget
Keys the project by the nearest .o2b-vault.json pointer, the harness by o2b mcp --harness, host by device id
Edits the vault-wide or one scoped file byte for byte with o2b brain standing-rules show, set or clear
Writes the store's standing-rule lane with human authority on a machine switched to the brain store
Refuses agent writes: note tools reject Brain/ paths and brain_labels has a named guard for these files
limits: Harness files apply only through brain_context; the session hooks carry no harness identity
No MCP tool writes the rules; they change only through the CLI verb or a file editor

features.name: Context packs
features.summary: Returns preference and retired-rule pages by tier and recency under a token budget, with presets and a size report.
capabilities: Packs preference and retired pages by tier, newest first, until the ceil(bytes/4) estimate hits max_tokens
Derives max_tokens from the model window (context.window_tokens, env, model table, 1m suffix) via a preset
Filters by query substring, or orders by token overlap (ranked) or stored belief vectors (semantic)
Caps characters per page and in total, cutting hard or in stages (`recall.degradation`)
Splits items into directive, constraint and consider lanes on request
Shows, suggests or diffs read-only presets tight-context (4000 tokens) and long-context (24000 tokens)
Advises strategy, budget split, graph hops and a marginal-value stop per question, writing nothing
Reports token totals of Brain/ pages per category against a warn threshold (default 200000)
limits: Packs preference and retired-rule pages only, not notes, sources or session history
Semantic order needs stored belief vectors and refuses when no page in reach has one
Refuses an unplaced model id unless max_tokens or context.window_tokens is given; no silent default
The score-aware tail trim runs only in brain_context_pack, behind tail_trim_context_pack (default off)

features.name: Prompt-time recall injection
features.summary: Optional hooks inject a bounded recall brief per prompt or a link-graph map on a cadence, plus a warm session cache.
capabilities: With recall_inject_enabled (default off), injects matching note titles, paths, spans and scores per prompt
Caps the brief at 4 notes, 900 chars and 2500 ms; abstains below 0.35 IDF-weighted query coverage
Skips notes the session already saw in the start digest or an earlier brief (recall_inject_dedupe, on)
Retrieves named slices (path prefix, types, limit, chars) declared in the recall_inject block of _brain.yaml
With the recall_inject decision-model use in enforce, drops notes or withholds the brief; shadow only records
With nav_tier_enabled (default off), injects vault size and the top 8 hubs by link degree every 30 minutes
Warms an anticipatory pack plus session hits (2000 tokens, 120 s TTL) on prompt and tool events
Reads that cache by session lineage root as warm, stale or miss through brain_anticipatory_context
limits: Fails closed: an error or timeout injects nothing, and the decision is audited with counts and scores only
Uses the existing cross-vault search without its decision-model rerank; adds no retriever of its own
No hook injects the anticipatory cache; agents read it through the tool or brain anticipate

features.name: Cross-agent catch-up
features.summary: Shows a session what other agents and machines recorded on its topics and in the shared log since it last looked.
capabilities: Reads topic records appended to the brain store's shards since the session's last prompt, via a byte cursor
Keeps decision, question, milestone, status and log records on the session's topics or in its project
Drops the session's own records by a session stamp (sha256 of the session id), else by device and agent
Passes a record when the session works on its topic and its kind is decision, refined by `neighbour_relevant`
Injects at most 5 fenced lines sharing 800 chars before the turn, one heading per topic
Is on by default with a brain store; neighbour_updates_enabled false turns it off
With log_catchup_enabled (default off), injects other agents' Brain/log lines at session start, newest 50
Keeps a per-identity watermark per log shard, so each foreign line shows once, attributed to its agent
limits: Neighbour updates read only the brain store's topics shards; a vault without a store gets none
A session's first prompt, and the first after a day idle, only place the cursor and inject nothing
A turn cut by the hook ceiling shows nothing and moves no cursor; its updates come on the next turn
Log catch-up identifies itself by agent name or device id; with neither it stays silent

features.name: Compaction survival
features.summary: Builds a pre-compression rules addendum, extracts labelled lines before compaction and re-asserts drifted pins after.
capabilities: Returns the top-K (default 10) confirmed preferences by confidence plus the head of active.md as an addendum
Caps the addendum per entry and in total, deriving the caps from the resolved model window when not given
Extracts 'Label: body' lines (label at most 3 words, 32 chars, any script) as pre_compact_extract records
Dedupes extracted records by session, turn range, label and content hash
Finds the last summary marker and keyword-probes each pinned line in the active versus the summary region
Appends drifted anchors to pinned context as a re-assertion block, once per session and summary hash
Runs the post-compaction audit only with post_compact_survival_audit on (default off) or --force
limits: The audit recognizes only the three built-in summary markers of the Hermes compressor
No shipped hook runs the audit; a host pipes {session_id, messages} JSON to the CLI verb
Extraction is called by the Hermes plugin and the Aider wrapper; the Claude Code and Codex hooks never call it

features.name: Context receipts and outcomes
features.summary: Records what context was delivered, whether it was used, its token impact and generation usage, and joins them by id.
capabilities: Appends a context_receipt per session-start injection: per-source bytes, tokens, budget and sha256 hashes
Writes receipts for context and pre-compress packs only when the call passes receipt: true
Lists, shows, folds a window into a retrieval summary, or re-hashes a receipt against the vault (verify)
Joins a receipt to its session's quote-check verdicts by exact session_id, or names it unjoined
Traces a Brain log event to its continuity records by session, turn or artifact correlation ids
Stores host-given USED, IGNORED or CONTRADICTED verdicts per injected memory for observed-reuse ranking
Ledgers token impact, pack outcomes and generation usage, each behind its own config key (default off)
Exports continuity records as ATOF or ATIF v1.7 trajectories (`brain continuity export`)
limits: The kernel computes no observed-use verdict; the host must supply them
Token figures are caller-reported or the ceil(bytes/4) estimate; the ledgers verify neither
Receipt verify runs at local reach only and refuses private or redacted receipts
